analysis.title: Fed Thoughts: Climbing Up the Learning Curve
key_insights: BNY expects the Fed to raise rates at least one more time this year under Chair Kevin Warsh, less than five months into the job.
Warsh tends to avoid forward guidance, so BNY expects no signal of the decision going into the October meeting.
BNY expects the Fed to present a firm stance on price stability, giving its message a hawkish skew.

BNY is uncertain about the cadence of policy action. The committee leans toward removing accommodation, but Warsh proposed cutting the annual number of scheduled meetings and may prefer less frequent interventions.
Warsh places greater faith in market mechanisms. BNY says he would rather learn from investors than lead them and worries less about high-frequency data fluctuations.

When inflation is far from the 2 percent goal, the policy direction is clearer and forward guidance helps anchor expectations. When inflation is near goal, the tradeoff is more delicate and the Fed should refrain from guidance to get a clean read of market views.

Warsh's September press conference summary was: trends matter, data points are noisy, data dependence is a dangerous preoccupation. He still appears comfortable with gradual 25-basis-point adjustments.
BNY argues an eighteen-month outlook is unlikely to change in the six weeks between FOMC meetings. Once adjustments begin, momentum continues, which is why BNY expects further hikes this year.
Warsh has asked the Committee to consider fewer regularly scheduled meetings. This would raise the institutional hurdle for frequent adjustments without necessarily meaning fewer policy actions.

BNY puts the chance of an October hike higher than markets price, since action would reinforce his price-stability commitment, show all meetings are live, and deliver another blow to forward guidance.
BNY's base case is that medium-termism wins and the hike is deferred to December, but it says it cannot say for certain.

BNY believes Warsh sees the world as in the latter, flatter part of the policy terrain, where listening to markets makes more sense than leading them. Some colleagues view that area as more circumscribed and share their policy views in public.

macro_indicators.reading: At least one more rate increase in 2026
macro_indicators.interpretation: BNY expects further tightening, with the October hike possible but December the base case.
The further inflation is from goal, the greater the loss to society, and the loss rises quickly away from 2 percent.
With the labor market balanced, the policy calculation depends mainly on inflation's distance from goal.

risk_factors: Uncertain cadence of Fed action: an October hike versus deferral to December.
Warsh's rejection of forward guidance reduces signaling, raising the odds of surprise at meetings.
Committee members may share policy views in public that differ from the chair's, adding mixed messaging.
vol_and_positioning: BNY puts the chances of an October Fed hike higher than currently priced in markets, though it says the base case is deferral to December.

key_data_points.metric: Size of gradual policy adjustments Warsh appears comfortable with
key_data_points.context: Gradual adjustment size BNY expects the Fed to use
key_data_points.anchor: he also seems comfortable with gradual 25-basis-point policy adjustments

key_data_points.context: Inflation goal in the Fed's dual mandate
key_data_points.anchor: keeping employment at its maximum sustainable level and inflation at the goal of 2 percent

key_data_points.metric: Number of regularly scheduled FOMC meetings BNY says may be too many
key_data_points.context: Warsh said at confirmation hearings that four is not enough
key_data_points.anchor: “Four is not enough,” but it seems that eight may be too many.

tension_points.bull_case: An October hike would reinforce Warsh's commitment to price stability, show all meetings are live, and deliver another blow to forward guidance, so BNY puts the odds higher than markets price.
tension_points.bear_case: Medium-termism and a preference for fewer interventions could win out, with action deferred to December.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Warsh heads into the October meeting with no firm plan to raise rates, and the 'family discussion' at the meeting does not tip the scales toward action.

theme_stances.key_argument: Once a policy adjustment begins, momentum takes over, so the Fed is likely to raise rates further this year.
theme_stances.evidence: we believe that the Fed is likely to raise rates further this year

theme_stances.key_argument: Warsh prefers to learn from markets rather than influence them, so the Fed should refrain from guidance when inflation is near goal.
theme_stances.evidence: Forward guidance is not the business we should be in.
